title: Trading Places
tagline: One dollar bet. One very big swap.
about: Two rich brothers make a bet that swaps a snob and a street hustler's lives.
cue: Serve the mains during the New Year's Eve train party.
faces: The Dining Room, Christmas week, 1983. Luncheon from noon, dinner from six.
Prunes stuffed with a whole almond, rolled in Lancaster bacon and baked crisp.
Philadelphia’s own, dark and peppery, with sherry poured at the table.
Six jumbo Gulf shrimp chilled on cracked ice, sharp red sauce and lemon.
Cos, coddled egg, anchovy and Parmesan, dressed at your table.
THE HERITAGE CLUB, DINNER FROM SIX
The front hall. Every guest is signed in by a member.
Standing rib, salted a day ahead, roasted slow and carved to order.
Natural juices, horseradish cream, browned potatoes.
Ask for the end cut early.
Lump blue crab, barely bound, browned in butter. Tartar sauce, lemon.
Whole, browned in butter and boned at the table. Parsley potatoes.
Grated rind and juice in the batter, brushed warm with orange syrup.
Fresh-squeezed juice and chilled champagne, half and half.
Vodka and orange juice whirled with ice. Never concentrate.
THE HOUSE COMMITTEE. Members may wager on any subject, provided it is entered in the Book.
Prices subject to change. Private parties in the Harvard Room. Form HC-23, 1983.

    StartersDevils on horsebackPrunes stuffed with a whole almond, rolled in Lancaster bacon and baked crisp.Opening Bell, served warm.How to make it20 pitted prunes20 almonds10 rashers of streaky baconPush an almond into each prune.Wrap each in half a rasher of bacon and secure with a toothpick.Bake at 200°C until the bacon is crisp.Serve warm.Caesar saladCos, coddled egg, anchovy and Parmesan, dressed at your table.Louis Winthorpe’s usual, before the bet.How to make it2 cos lettuces200g sourdough loaf40g butter1 egg2 garlic cloves6 anchovy fillets1 lemon1 tsp Worcestershire sauce1 tsp Dijon mustard80ml olive oil60g parmesanTear the sourdough into small pieces and fry in the butter, tossing, until golden and crisp. Drain.Lower the egg into simmering water for 1 minute, then cool it under the tap.Mash the garlic and anchovies to a paste in a big bowl. Crack in the coddled egg, add the lemon juice, Worcestershire and mustard, then whisk in the oil slowly until thick.Add the cos leaves, whole or torn, and toss at the table until every leaf is coated.Shave the parmesan over, scatter the croutons and serve straight away.MainsRoast prime rib of beefStanding rib, salted a day ahead, roasted slow and carved to order. Natural juices, horseradish cream, browned potatoes.Ask for the end cut early.How to make it2kg standing rib roast2 tbsp salt300ml beef stock150g horseradish cream1kg potatoes, in chunks3 tbsp oil for the potatoesSalt the roast the day before and leave it uncovered in the fridge.Roast at 120°C until 52°C inside.Rest the beef.Roast the potatoes in oil at 200°C while the beef rests.Blast the beef at 260°C for a crust.Simmer the pan juices with the stock for jus.Carve and serve with horseradish cream, potatoes and jus.SweetsOrange butter cakeGrated rind and juice in the batter, brushed warm with thick orange syrup.The Closing Bell.How to make it200g butter, softened250g caster sugar2 oranges, zested3 eggs250g self-raising flour100ml orange juice100ml orange juice concentrateBeat the butter, most of the sugar and the orange zest until pale.Add the eggs, then fold in the flour with the orange juice.Bake in a lined tin at 170°C.Boil the concentrate with the remaining sugar and brush over the warm cake.DrinksMimosaFresh-squeezed juice and chilled champagne, half and half.From the Members' Bar.How to make it4 oranges, about 300ml juice300ml chilled sparkling wineSqueeze the oranges and chill the juice well.Fill four flutes halfway with juice and gently top with sparkling wine, pouring slowly.
